This study investigates the application of the Novikov density method in pricing options on assets subject to downward-bounded price constraints. This research examines whether standard risk-neutral measures that satisfy no--arbitrage and a martingale property can support the pricing of such options using this method. It is demonstrated that this property fails, and as a result, a revised model is proposed, incorporating a new probability measure that meets the required criteria. Furthermore, a detailed derivation of the risk-neutral density function is presented for a range of standard models, including Black--Scholes, Merton, and VaCa models. This analysis is then extended to a broader class of models, and numerical simulations are performed to demonstrate the effect of the no--arbitrage property on European option pricing. Finally, an extension to European-style options with multiple underlying assets is presented, and a numerical algorithm is developed to solve the resulting problem. This research offers a practical framework for the risk-neutral pricing of assets subject to downward-bounded price constraints. This is particularly relevant in the context of cryptocurrency options, where the absence of a central clearing house necessitates the application of risk-neutral measures that preserve the arbitrage property. This study provides a comprehensive solution to the resulting challenges. The research is presented in three papers, each focusing on a specific aspect: the first paper addresses the no--arbitrage property, the second explores the pricing of options on assets subject to downward-bounded price constraints, and the third discusses the effects on European option pricing and the extension to options on multiple assets. This report presents the findings of the research, highlighting the key results. The accompanying software is freely available on GitHub at https://github.com/ferancatala/risk-neutral-density.
